old_description: Custom Wire Industries, Inc. is a UL and CSA certified manufacturer of
about:
Custom Wire Industries, Inc. was founded in 1968 in Muskego, Wisconsin. The company has operated continuously from its Wisconsin base for over five decades.

The company manufactures electrical wire and cable assemblies, wire harnesses, ribbon cables, overmolded assemblies, lead wires, electromechanical devices, control panels, power transmission assemblies, and sensor cables. Its capabilities span cable fabrication, wire harness assembly, electromechanical assembly, custom tooling, injection molding, CAD-based design, kitting, and turnkey system integration. Assemblies range from microscopic components to 900-pound alert tower units. The engineering team uses a fully capable CAD system to generate working drawings and provide design services.

Custom Wire Industries serves medical, military, industrial, telecommunications, and automotive sectors. Customers include OEMs and manufacturers requiring custom cable assemblies for equipment such as diagnostic medical devices, military-spec power systems, and industrial control panels. The company emphasizes consolidated sourcing, allowing clients to purchase all components together to reduce shipping and labor costs.

The company highlights its UL and CSA certifications, strict quality control processes at each manufacturing stage, and a commitment to 100% quality management. It promotes affordable pricing, fast turnaround times, and low defect rates as key differentiators. Since its founding, it has focused on delivering customized electromechanical assemblies, control panels, and power cable assemblies tailored to exact specifications.

name: Cutlist CO
old_description: Precision CNC ROUTING AND LASER CUTTING for ARTISTS, MAKERS, BUILDERS AND DESIGNERS.
about:
Cutlist CO operates as a digital fabrication studio in Denver, Colorado. The company was founded in 2006 and has accumulated two decades of experience in precision cutting services.

The shop provides CNC routing and laser cutting services using a ShopSabre CNC router equipped with a 12-position automatic tool changer and vacuum hold-down, plus a pro-series laser cutter and 3D printing capabilities. It processes full 48-by-96-inch sheets, handling 2D profiles, dados, pockets, drill patterns, laser cutting, engraving, and nested part optimization for batch runs of 500 pieces or more. Most jobs are completed within 10 business days.

Customers include artists, makers, builders, designers, woodworkers, and small businesses across sectors such as art installations, interior design, furniture, cabinetry, custom shelving, prototypes, models, jigs, storage solutions, signage, marketing components, and retail displays. The company accepts DXF, SVG, 3D CAD models, and dimensioned drawings, converting them into cut files while leaving design work to the client.

Cutlist CO differentiates itself by focusing solely on cutting—delivering clean, precise parts ready for customer finishing and assembly—and by sourcing materials directly to ensure consistent quality, flatness, and machine compatibility. A $500 job minimum applies to CNC routing, and the studio offers local delivery for larger orders while maintaining a pickup-only policy for most work.

D.W. Woodcraft, Inc. operates from Ava, Missouri, where it was founded in 1983 by David and Julie Rust Posey. The business initially produced kitchen and bath cabinets alongside furniture and novelty items.

The company specializes in custom woodworking for residential spaces, producing kitchen cabinets, bathroom vanities, entertainment centers, bookshelves, desks, armoires, and other built-in furniture. A computer-aided design and cut-list system has been in use since 1990, supporting precise estimation and fabrication. The operation moved to a larger facility on Highway 5 South in 1993, which includes a showroom described as the largest in the area. At its peak, the shop employed nine craftsmen.

D.W. Woodcraft serves homeowners, remodelers, and new-construction clients throughout the region. Projects range from complete kitchen and bathroom remodels to custom entertainment walls and standalone furniture pieces. The firm emphasizes a consultative approach, offering free estimates and showroom appointments to select materials such as mahogany and maple.

The Posey family’s involvement spans generations; David’s son Daniel worked in the shop during high school. The company states its goal is to deliver the highest quality craftsmanship on every project, relying on close collaboration with clients to achieve a “wow” factor in each finished piece.

DK Fabrication and Welding operates from Tollesboro, Kentucky, where it has been running as a business for five years. The company is certified as a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) and is also family-owned, reflecting a blend of military discipline and family values in its operations.

The shop provides custom, structural, ornamental, and industrial metal fabrication, working with steel, stainless steel, aluminum, and specialty alloys across a range of material thicknesses. Core processes include CNC plasma cutting, press brake forming, MIG and TIG welding, and aluminum and structural steel fabrication, enabling both large-scale and intricate projects.

While construction is a primary market, the company also serves automotive, oil and gas, residential, commercial, and industrial sectors, and its SAM.gov registration allows it to pursue government contracts alongside private work.

The firm emphasizes its veteran-owned, family-operated identity as a differentiator, citing 18 years of hands-on fabrication experience, state-of-the-art CNC plasma and press brake equipment, and a commitment to being fully licensed, insured, and certified for every job.

old_description: We are a national wholesale manufacturer of hospitality drapery, multi-housing and commercial draperies and bedding.
about:
Drapery Manufacturing Inc., doing business as DMI Wholesale Textile, was founded in 1975 in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The company operates a 32,000-square-foot manufacturing facility centrally located in the United States, allowing it to service customers nationwide.

The company custom manufactures draperies, curtains, bedding, and window-treatment hardware for hospitality, multi-housing, commercial, and healthcare markets. Its turnkey service includes professional field measuring, manufacturing, and installation. Capabilities cover hospitality drapes, multi-housing window coverings, commercial and office draperies, hospital cubicle and privacy curtains, food-service curtains, grommet draperies, valances, cornices, Roman and flat-fold shades, solar shades, wood blinds, and a range of hardware such as Graber tracks, wrought-iron rods, and cubicle track systems. DMI also offers COM (customer’s own material) labor and sources fabrics from major suppliers.

Primary customers include interior designers, decorators, hotel and motel operators, university and apartment housing managers, healthcare facility administrators, nursing homes, clinics, and food-service establishments. The firm has supplied window coverings for hotel renovations, university dormitories, hospital privacy curtains, and restaurant kitchen partitions.

DMI emphasizes its 1975 founding, a solid Dun & Bradstreet credit history, and a commitment to never delaying a grand opening. It sells wholesale to the trade only, offers competitive pricing, and ensures all custom draperies are tabled for size with lined top-treatment boards. Flame-retardant hospital curtains meet NFPA 701 standards, and the company can supply any fabric or work with customer-provided material.

name: DN Plastics
old_description: Manufacturing Engineered Thermoplastic Compounds, Sheets and Gels
about:
DN Plastics was founded in 1998 in Morrison, Tennessee, as a family-owned business. The company is certified as a Women-Owned Minority Business Enterprise.

The company manufactures engineered thermoplastic compounds, sheets, and gels, operating six compounding lines — four Coperion 70 mm twin-screw and two single-screw extruders — with a combined capacity exceeding 100 million pounds per year. Its 120,000-square-foot facility includes a sheet extrusion line capable of producing up to 90-inch-wide sheet with co-extrusion and lamination capabilities, and is served by rail for bulk logistics. DN Plastics also offers toll compounding, new product development, and analytical testing services from a laboratory equipped with FTIR, DSC, TGA, and DMA instruments.

Its customer base spans automotive and non-automotive sectors. Automotive applications include interior trim components, door panels, cowl-vent grilles, blow-molded air ducts, engine covers, dash insulators, door insulators, flooring insulators, non-carpeted flooring, and cargo van liners. Non-automotive markets served include sporting goods, toys, wire and cable, healthcare products, household appliances, furniture, and general household items.

DN Plastics emphasizes its state-of-the-art equipment, scalable capacity, strategic rail access, advanced laboratory capabilities, ISO 9001 registration, and a sustainability focus that integrates post-consumer and post-industrial recycled materials into closed-loop recycling programs.

about:
Dakota Emporium Trading Post has operated from Fort Pierre, South Dakota since 1926. The business occupies a storefront and is run by proprietor Mike, who also travels to regional powwows with inventory.

The trading post stocks a wide range of Native American craft supplies, including seed beads, regalia components, jewelry findings, drum-making materials, tanned hides, quillwork, and botanicals. It also carries finished Native-made jewelry and artwork. Operations are centered on a single retail location, with additional sales conducted at events across the region.

The store serves Native American artisans, powwow dancers, cultural practitioners, and hobbyists seeking authentic materials for traditional and contemporary craftwork. Customers include individuals preparing regalia for ceremonies, as well as collectors of Native-made artwork.

The company emphasizes personal service and competitive pricing, with the proprietor known for traveling to meet customers at powwows and other gatherings.

Dakota Fabrication Inc. was incorporated in February 2006 in Harrisburg, South Dakota, initially specializing in stainless steel pipe fabrication for the ethanol industry. The company has since expanded its capabilities to include carbon steel, aluminum, and alloy piping and structural steel fabrication.

The facility includes lay-down area for project materials and finished items awaiting shipment.

The company serves ethanol plants, power generation facilities, mining operations, and food-grade sectors including dairy, beverage, brewing, distillery, medical, and vaccine production. Past clients include Midwestern Mechanical, Mechanical Solutions LLC, and 9 Clouds, with testimonials citing on-schedule delivery, work quality, and QA/QC performance.

Founded to address the ethanol industry's need for specialized stainless pipe fabrication, Dakota Fabrication maintains an ISO-like quality program following its 2011 ISO 9001:2008 ANAB registration, emphasizing precision, experience, and responsive on-site service.

about:
Fairfield Manufacturing operates its primary North American production hub in Lafayette, Indiana. The company traces its origins to 1919, establishing a century-long focus on custom gears and drive systems.

The Lafayette campus spans 60,000 square meters and houses more than 600 machine tools and 60 furnaces, with 7,000 square meters dedicated to heat treatment. In-house capabilities cover the full product lifecycle: engineering and design (including reverse engineering and clean-sheet development), gear cutting (external, internal, high-speed, planetary, hypoid, and Zerol configurations), shaft machining, heat treating (carburizing, annealing, nitriding, induction), precision machining (drilling, milling, tapping, sawing), metallurgical testing, failure analysis, product performance validation in lab and field, and large-scale assembly and inspection. Gear quality is certified to AGMA Class 14.

Global original equipment manufacturers in marine, mining, oil and gas, railway, environment, energy, recycling, and construction equipment (including compact track loaders) rely on Fairfield for integrated gear production. The plant produces Spicer Torque-Hub track drives and other large components such as bull gears, pinions, and starter gears for on- and offshore applications.

Fairfield differentiates itself through fully integrated, in-house control of design, manufacturing, testing, and certification, backed by approvals from the American Bureau of Shipping, Lloyd’s Register, the Association of American Railroads, DNV, and the Performance Review Institute. Its engineering team specializes in resolving gear noise, heat, vibration, and early-failure issues, offering both build-to-print and complete solution services.

Daniels Manufacturing Corporation (DMC) is headquartered in Orlando, Florida. The company traces its roots to 1947 when founder Bill Daniels began a general job-shop in Pontiac, Michigan, producing components for automotive manufacturers such as Ford. Incorporated in 1949 in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan, DMC is a veteran-owned small business that emphasizes a family culture across its operations.

DMC designs and manufactures precision crimp tools, connector assembly tool kits, wire preparation tools, and specialty products including Safe-T-Cable® and LaceLok® for mission-critical electrical systems. The company operates a state-of-the-art facility with dozens of modern machines and maintains a global distributor network in more than 35 countries; many of its tools appear on the Department of Defense Qualified Product List (QPL).

DMC serves government and defense (ground, naval, aviation, space), commercial aviation (OEM, MRO, eVTOL, rotorcraft, airlines), space (satellites, launch vehicles), medical device manufacturers, telecommunications (military and RF wireless networks), automotive (OEM, motorsport, off-highway), rail (wayside, locomotive), power generation (hydro, solar, wind, nuclear), and automation (mining, robotics).

The company states its differentiation lies in its veteran-owned, family-culture foundation; AS9100D and ISO 9001:2015 certification; a nationwide team of field experts who visit customer facilities; active participation in industry standards bodies; and a commitment to custom solutions when standard tooling does not exist.

The company ships to more than 15 countries and supports OEM replacement parts, maintenance, and new product development.

about:
Double H Packaging, Inc. operates from its headquarters in Warminster, Pennsylvania, with additional manufacturing facilities in Marion, Indiana, and Morristown, Tennessee. The company was founded in 1974 by Harry Harp as a family-owned profile extrusion business producing plastic cores for the paper converting industry. It remains family-owned today.

The company produces a range of packaging products including cups and composite lids, thin-wall plastic containers, plastic cores, tubing, rails, and paper-based packaging. Its capabilities span profile extrusion, injection molding (thin-wall, insert, and cup forming), in-mold labeling, flexographic and offset printing, and in-house prototyping using stereolithography and powder printing. Tooling and mold making are performed internally, supported by a tool room and machine center across its three plants.

Double H serves primarily the food packaging sector, supplying snacks and convenience foods, ice cream and frozen desserts, and other food packaging applications. It also serves the paper converting industry with plastic cores and provides filtration packaging components. Customers include brands seeking custom packaging solutions tailored to specific branding and performance requirements.

The company emphasizes its ability to deliver custom solutions through in-house design, prototyping, and tooling, enabling fast, precise development. Its history includes pioneering a patented lid molding process in 1985 and, more recently, introducing a plastic-free All Paper Pint in 2025. Double H holds SQF certification for food safety.

The business, now based in Palatine, Illinois, remains family-owned and operated by the third generation, with Ed Eidenberg serving as the primary consultant and face of the company.

The company supplies new and used restaurant equipment, carrying brands such as John Boos, and provides design services that include AutoCAD-based floor layouts, equipment specifications, plumbing and electrical rough-in drawings, ventilation specifications, and 3D renderings. Ed and his team conduct on-site consultations within 24 hours, assist with delivery and installation, and have equipped more than 1,000 restaurants, bars, and hotels across the Chicago area and nationally.

Customers range from first-time restaurateurs to established operators expanding or renovating kitchens, as well as architects and foodservice consultants who collaborate on layout and compliance. The firm also serves convenience stores and other commercial foodservice segments.

The business was built on the founder's vision of personal, budget-friendly service, a principle the company says it maintains through hands-on expertise, 24/7 support, and a commitment to guiding clients through equipment selection without the guesswork of self-service purchasing.

EMSCO operates from Ashland, Virginia, providing on-demand electronics manufacturing for businesses across the mid-Atlantic and nationwide. The company positions itself as a local alternative to offshore production, emphasizing proximity and speed for regional customers.

The shop produces electrical wire and multi-conductor cable harnesses, printed circuit board assemblies, and electronic and mechanical box builds. Its floor includes in-motion continuity testing equipment, and work follows ISO 9001:2015-based procedures alongside IPC/WHMA-A 620 standards. A reported $500,000 of standing raw inventory supports short material lead times, and a near-zero voluntary attrition rate keeps experienced technicians on the line.

EMSCO serves Virginia- and mid-Atlantic-based companies that need fast, lower-cost shipping, while also shipping to the broader United States.

The firm states it was started to give customers scalable capacity without new infrastructure or headcount, claiming 10–50 percent savings on brand-name components through bulk purchasing and reduced lead times via its stocking programs.

old_description: EPE helps OEMs, EMS providers, and global supply chains recover value from excess, obsolete, and slow-moving electronic components through transparent resale and inventory recovery programs.
about:
Based in Salem, Massachusetts, Electronic Parts Exchange (EPE) operates as a specialist in excess electronic component recovery. The company serves original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), electronics manufacturing services (EMS) providers, and global supply chains.

EPE converts idle inventory into working capital through consignment or buyout programs, secure authorized remarketing, ESG circular reporting, and lifecycle obsolescence management. A proprietary ClearView platform tracks quotes, sales activity, balances, and recovery performance. The company also provides quality testing services including documentation inspection, external visual inspection, X-ray inspection (X6600/X6600B), solderability testing (MUST System 3), decapsulation (JetEtch), and Keyence microscopy up to 6000× magnification.

Customers span automotive, aviation/military, and medical sectors. The aviation and military segment is supported by AS9120B:2016 certification and DOD-certified test facilities. Medical clients receive semiconductors and LCDs sourced through strict vendor screening and quality control.

The company emphasizes a transparent recovery process, certified compliance (ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, AS9120B:2016), global resale reach, and consignment strategies that often outperform liquidation. Its quality system is AS6081 compliant for counterfeit detection, with rigorous external visual inspection on all incoming and outgoing shipments.

ES Solar is based in Layton, Utah, and was founded in 2010. The company operates as a solar panel and battery backup installer, managing projects from design through installation and ongoing service with a single in-house team.

The company provides residential and commercial solar installations, battery storage systems, and ongoing service and support. Since its founding, ES Solar has completed more than 15,000 installations across Utah, Nevada, California, Idaho, and Texas. Its service offering includes an 8-point system check, performance monitoring, and a Protection Plus plan that provides 100% service coverage. The firm also handles permitting and offers financing options such as cash purchase, prepaid lease, power purchase agreements, and loans.

ES Solar serves homeowners seeking energy independence and lower utility bills, as well as business owners aiming to reduce operating costs through commercial solar arrays. The company's residential customers are located in the five western states where it operates, while its commercial clients include businesses looking for clean, renewable power solutions.

ES Solar emphasizes its end-to-end in-house approach, which it says ensures accountability from design to activation. The company backs its installations with OEM warranties on parts and highlights its 100% customer satisfaction goal, supported by thousands of positive customer reviews.

about:
Eagle Automotive Distributors operates as part of the Lowe Automotive Group, headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri. The business traces its roots to 1968 when Norman Lowe established the company; after his passing in 1996, his son Jeff Lowe assumed the presidency of Lowe Automotive Whse. and MAP Automotive Whse. The group has grown through a series of expansions and acquisitions across Missouri, Illinois, and Wisconsin.

The company functions as a full-line warehouse distributor (Parts Plus WD) for automotive aftermarket parts. It stocks and supplies a broad range of components including S.U.R.&R. vehicle fluid line repair solutions for A/C, brake, and fuel lines. Operations span more than a dozen locations — among them Jefferson County Auto Parts in Arnold, Pevely Plaza Auto Parts, St Peters Auto Parts, South County and South Town Auto Parts in St. Louis, Eagle West in Ballwin, Lowe/Eagle Springfield, SEMO Automotive in Cape Girardeau, and MAP/Eagle sites in Milwaukee, Bloomington, Chicago, and Peoria. The group also acquired the parts division of Mid-Nite Automotive's jobber store in St. Peters in August 2023.

Customers include professional installers, independent repair shops, and Ford dealerships across the Midwest. The distributor supports Ford dealers through a dedicated Ford WebShop portal, while other buyers access inventory via the Connection, EPN (formerly AconneX), and Parts Tech electronic ordering platforms. St. Charles County installers and Wisconsin-based jobbers are specifically noted as key customer groups.

Leadership emphasizes that continued expansion remains "customer service driven." The company differentiates itself with a multi-channel ordering suite — WebDocs for document lookup, E-Statements, and three electronic ordering systems — alongside a wide brick-and-mortar footprint that puts inventory close to the shops it serves.

name: Eartec Co Inc
about:
Founded in 1961 in Narragansett, Rhode Island, Eartec Co Inc (originally operating as the Eartec/Porta Phone Company) began supplying headset communication systems to industries worldwide. The company remains based in Narragansett.

Eartec designs and manufactures a range of wireless and wired communication products. Its portfolio includes the UltraLITE and UltraLITE PRO16 series of full-duplex wireless intercoms using DECT and frequency-hopping technology, the Blackmagic Interface adapter for wired intercom integration, the SCRAMBLER Plus two-way radio system with encrypted signals, the TCS Wired industrial-grade wired intercom line, and the E-Pak digital wireless platform. The company also operates as the sole authorized repair center for its own brands in the United States.

The systems serve a diverse set of sectors: broadcast and stage production, commercial drone (UAS) operations, equestrian instruction, marine captain-to-crew communication, radio-controlled racing, restaurant and food-service operations, sailing, non-commercial cafeteria environments, and light industrial sites where wireless equipment is restricted. Customers purchase directly from the factory or through authorized dealers, with international distribution handled via a global partner network.

Eartec emphasizes customer service as a core differentiator, offering expert pre-sale advice, post-warranty support, and typical order shipping within one to three business days. The company positions itself as a long-term partner, highlighting transparency and accessibility throughout the product lifecycle.

name: Eastman Screen Printing
old_description: Founded in 2022, Eastman Screen Printing was a dream long in the making…
about:
Eastman Screen Printing was founded in 2022 in Concord, New Hampshire, as a locally owned shop. The venture began as a long-held dream of managers Ron Dulong and Sam Mostue, who envisioned a neighborhood screen-printing service where customers could watch their promotional products being crafted by hand, much like a local candy shop.

The company provides screen printing on apparel and tote bags using plastisol, water-based, and discharge inks; embroidery with digitizing, 3D foam, and puff styles; signs, banners, and vehicle graphics printed on vinyl; and business printing including cards, brochures, flyers, and direct-mail services such as EDDM. name: EcoGen America
old_description: Founded in 2016, we have expanded from regional roots to a nationwide data-driven platform, accumulating nearly a decade of direct solar industry exposure.
about:
EcoGen America is headquartered in Camden, Delaware, and was founded in 2016 by Trevor Guilday. The company began as a regional effort to connect homeowners with local solar installers and expanded nationwide by 2022 to cover all 50 states, Washington, D.C., and Puerto Rico. In 2025 the platform was completely rebuilt with a homeowner-first brand, strict verification frameworks, and updated data infrastructure. Leadership includes CEO Dean Mahmoud, who has worked in residential solar since 2021, and a core team overseeing data analytics, partnerships, technology, and content.

The company operates an independent solar education and research platform. It publishes the EcoGen Solar Cost Index, a state-level price benchmark built on Department of Energy laboratory benchmarks, Bureau of Labor Statistics wage data, Energy Information Administration electricity-use figures, and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory transacted-price data. The index is calibrated against current marketplace quotes and proprietary cost modeling. EcoGen also maintains a verified installer network; partners must hold an active state license, demonstrate installation activity in the state, and offer a workmanship warranty covering roof penetrations. The company processes quote requests from homeowners and earns referral fees from partner installers, while keeping editorial content independent of advertising relationships.

EcoGen serves residential homeowners exploring solar adoption across the United States. Its guides address system pricing, federal and state incentives, financing options, and installer selection. The platform’s matching service connects homeowners with solar providers in their area; as of September 2026 the network included six commercial partners. The company’s data and methodology are referenced by contributing experts in solar policy, tax credits, and clean energy journalism.

EcoGen was created to close a transparency gap in the solar industry, where homeowners faced high-pressure sales tactics without reliable, unbiased data. The founder’s stated goal is to provide free educational resources, up-to-date pricing insights, and personalized quote comparisons so that homeowners know exactly what they are buying before signing a contract. The company emphasizes public data sources, a published verification methodology, and a revenue model that does not influence editorial recommendations.

A second 19,000-square-foot shop in Omaha, acquired in 2024, adds horizontal boring mills, larger-capacity lathes, surface and shaft grinding, broaching, and onsite machining and press repair services.

EleMETAL serves industrial and food manufacturing customers across the United States. Its client base includes companies needing custom-fabricated components, aftermarket replacement parts, and specialized equipment such as the company's own sanitary pivot dumpers. The team collaborates on design through final fabrication, leveraging a large raw-material inventory to reduce lead times.

The business was built on a passion for quality and fair pricing, a legacy the current owners say continues to drive their focus on solving customer problems quickly with skilled engineers, fabricators, and machinists.

name: EnaChip Inc.
old_description: In 2013 he returned to Penn to become the Alfred Fitler Moore Professor and Director of Penn’s Singh Center for Nanotechnology. In 2024 he became Chair of Penn’s Department of Electrical and Systems Engineering. Mark’s research is in the area of microelectromechanical systems (MEMS). Beginning with a plenary address to the 1994 IEEE Applied Power Engineering Conference on the topic of integrated inductors, and continuing through today, a major thrust of his program is the realization of microfabricated magnetics for advanced power delivery. He has chaired or co-chaired multiple conferences and co-founded multiple MEMS companies.
about:
EnaChip Inc. is based in Rocky Hill, New Jersey. The company develops and manufactures magnetics for high-frequency power conversion, with a focus on AI data center infrastructure.

The company produces bespoke magnetics—including multilayer inductors and wafer-level arrays—that enable vertical power delivery for 800V DC architectures. Its fabrication process uses electroplating on standard semiconductor equipment to create thick copper planar windings and high-flux-density cores, achieving low DC resistance and efficient switching above 10 MHz. Devices range from single ~1 mm components to wafer-level arrays, integrating with GaN and advanced silicon switches.

EnaChip targets operators and designers of AI data centers and high-performance computing systems where power delivery losses are a primary constraint. Its technology addresses the last-centimeter conversion and routing losses between voltage regulators and processor dies. The company also lists energy harvesting and energy conversion among its served markets.

EnaChip states that its electroplated core stacks cut manufacturing time dramatically and that its parts drop into any level of a design stack—board, package, or die. The company emphasizes that power delivery should enable performance rather than limit it, positioning its magnetics as a way to unlock the capabilities of next-generation switches.

The firm emphasizes its status as one of the few remaining onshore apparel factories, marketing “Made in the USA” output. Differentiators include in‑house 3D rendering (rare in Maryland), digital pattern workflows that reduce sample iterations, and Spector’s 50‑plus years of industry experience guiding development and costing.

about:
Founded approximately 45 years ago in a church basement, the organization has grown into a statewide network.

The food bank distributes millions of pounds of food annually—including pantry staples and fresh produce from its own farms—through a network of over 600 partner agencies, mobile pantries, school backpack programs, and senior home deliveries. It also runs free accelerated job training programs in warehousing/logistics and food service, alongside nutrition education, financial coaching, SNAP outreach, and legislative advocacy.

The organization serves food-insecure individuals and families across Delaware, including children, seniors, and low-income neighborhoods. Its partner pantries, schools, and community agencies act as distribution points, while its workforce development programs target adults seeking employment in logistics and culinary fields.

The food bank’s stated mission is to inspire hope by addressing both immediate hunger and its root cause, poverty. It emphasizes compassion, respect, collaboration, empowerment, and innovation as core values, aiming to transform lives beyond temporary relief.

old_description: systems bring positive and dramatic changes to food manufacturing
about:
Food Physics was founded in 2012 in Boise, Idaho, and operates from facilities in Boise and Chelmsford, Essex, United Kingdom. The company was established to identify and maximize the potential of new technologies in the food and beverage industry.

The firm provides Pulsed Electric Field (PEF) systems for food processing as the sole North American, UK, and Irish distributor for Elea, the German manufacturer of the equipment. Food Physics customizes each PEF system to a client’s production line, offers pilot-scale testing at its partner facilities in the United States, Britain, and Germany, and supports installations with a spare-parts dispatch and field-service team. More than 100 PEF systems have been installed globally.

Customers span food and beverage processing, agricultural processing, and scientific research. Applications include potato-chip and french-fry production, freeze-drying, vegetable and fruit processing, winemaking, spirulina extraction for food and textile dyes, and dried-produce improvement. The company serves clients of all sizes across North America, the United Kingdom, and Ireland.

Food Physics emphasizes innovation, with over 17 PEF-related patents pending and collaborative R&D projects that drive new commercial applications. Its mission is to deliver systems that increase yield, improve product stability, and reduce waste, enabling products from freeze-dried foods to paints to reach the market efficiently.

name: Food Process Systems Inc
old_description: Since 1989, Food Process Systems has been designing and manufacturing innovative, Made-in-America food processing equipment that helps manufacturers improve productivity, sanitation, and worker safety.
about:
Food Process Systems Inc. is based in Lodi, Wisconsin, and has been designing and manufacturing food processing equipment since 1989. The company is veteran-owned and operated; in June 2025 it was acquired by Viper Engineering & Manufacturing LLC, a firm founded by Air Force veteran Brian J. Gilbertson. All customer-facing operations continue under the Food Process Systems name at the existing Lodi facility.

It also provides preventative maintenance, installation and commissioning, equipment audits, retrofits and upgrades, training, and 24/7 service and repair. Manufacturing takes place at its Lodi plant, where a team of engineers, technicians, and specialists supports equipment sold worldwide.

Food Process Systems serves poultry, seafood, meat, dairy, snack, packaging, cereal, pet food, produce, dry goods, baked goods, candy, and frozen-food processors. Its equipment is used by food manufacturers seeking to improve productivity, sanitation, and worker safety across those segments.

The company emphasizes engineering excellence, customer collaboration, and reliable performance, stating that its Made-in-America equipment helps processors meet production challenges with confidence. It prioritizes integrity and service, and notes that using original FPS parts preserves equipment warranties and compatibility.

about:
Food Processors Water Cooperative, Inc. (FPWC) operates as a public water supply in Timberville, Virginia. Founded in 1946, the cooperative is owned by Pilgrim's Pride Corporation and Cargill Meat Solutions. It began with four customers, one employee, 300,000 gallons of storage, 4,428 feet of distribution lines, and a treatment plant capable of 500,000 gallons per day.

The facility draws water from the North Fork of the Shenandoah River and employs the Roberts Filter Manhattan Process of High Rate filtration. Treatment steps include disinfection, coagulation, flocculation, sedimentation, and filtration through four mixed media filters running at 1,360 gallons per minute. Current capacity is 2,000,000 gallons per day with 3,300,000 gallons of storage across three tanks and 13,239 feet of underground distribution lines. Seven employees serve 28 bulk-use customers, delivering nearly 500 million gallons annually.

Primary customers include the two owning food manufacturers, Pilgrim's Pride and Cargill, as well as the Towns of Broadway and Timberville and other area businesses and residents. The cooperative provides potable water for food processing operations and municipal supply.

FPWC has earned multiple Excellence in Operations awards from the Virginia Department of Health, Office of Water Programs, recognizing its cross-connection control, financial management, water quality process control, distribution system management, and plant staffing and training. It is noted as the second oldest High Rate water treatment plant in Virginia.

about:
Food Service Specialties was founded in 1985 in Columbus, Wisconsin, by lifelong friends Don Leick and Steve Lineer. The pair started the business after a customer asked them to match and scale up a custom pizza sauce to achieve batch-to-batch consistency. The company remains family-owned, with the second generation now active in daily operations.

The firm formulates, manufactures, and customizes tomato- and dairy-based sauces for foodservice and retail channels. After outgrowing its original plant, FSS relocated to Red Wing, Minnesota, in 1998, constructing a 45,000-square-foot facility.

Leick and Lineer launched the business to solve a consistency problem in sauce production, and the company says its mission today is to deliver safe, legal, high-quality food products to the marketplace.

name: Food Solutions, Inc.
old_description: We’ve proudly owned and operated our 11,000 square-foot, federally-certified food facility and HQ in north-Denver since 2011. Our teams have imagined, prepared and delivered millions of units of private label, grab-and-go, quick serve and other food concepts for our clients and partners nationwide.
about:
Food Solutions, Inc. operates an 11,000-square-foot USDA-, FDA-, and SQF-certified food production facility and headquarters in north Denver, Colorado. The company traces its roots to 2006 when sister company Western Deli Provisions launched as a wholesale distributor of premium deli foods. In 2011 the current certified facility opened, and in 2015 Food Solutions was formed as a full-service co-manufacturer and prepared-foods producer under founder and president Steve Lederer.

The facility houses kettle cooking, smokehouse, and sausage manufacturing equipment, with a 30’x40’ production room, a 60’x40’ cook and raw production room, a 20’x40’ cooler with production space, a 10’x50’ freezer, and two drive-in delivery docks. The company provides end-to-end co-manufacturing services—recipe development, batching and scaling, labeling, production, fulfillment, and delivery—for private-label, grab-and-go, quick-serve, and other prepared food concepts. It reports having produced millions of units for clients nationwide.

Food Solutions serves executive chefs and culinary directors of hotels, resorts, and multi-unit restaurant operators, as well as food-industry entrepreneurs and early-stage ventures. Its Signature line of grab-and-go products is sold at airports (including Denver International Airport), education and healthcare institutions, and retail venues across the country. Regional and national food distributors also rely on the company for specialty food concepts and custom culinary services.

The company emphasizes a “work smart, work together, deliver delicious” philosophy and maintains SQF certification consistently above industry compliance levels, with mandatory annual third-party audits and unannounced audits every three years. It positions itself as a turn-key partner that handles everything from concept development through final delivery.
